title: Legora expands leading legal AI training program to the UK
summary: Legora today announced the expansion of its Legal AI Scholars Program to the United Kingdom, collaborating with leading UK law schools to integrate professional-grade legal AI across their programs.
body_markdown:
Legora today announced the expansion of its Legal AI Scholars Program to the United Kingdom, collaborating with leading UK law schools to integrate professional-grade legal AI across their programs. Applications range from embedding Legora across professional legal training to the work students are doing in the schools' pro bono legal clinics, where they use Legora to deliver real legal help to members of the community.


The founding UK members of the initiative are King's College London, The City Law School and BPP University Law School. Each school gains access to the same enterprise-grade Legora platform used by leading law firms and in-house legal teams worldwide, along with free student and faculty licenses and specialized training. Legora's dedicated law school team works directly with faculty to develop AI-focused instruction that pairs practical skills with ethical guardrails.


The UK is one of the first markets outside the United States to join the Legal AI Scholars Program, which launched in March with nine US law schools including Stanford, Northwestern and the University of Chicago. Its arrival is timely: in August the Solicitors Regulation Authority issued a formal warning notice on the misuse of AI, making clear that solicitors remain accountable for AI-assisted work and must be competent to supervise it. For law schools, AI literacy is becoming less elective and more of a professional obligation.


That shift is already reflected in how future solicitors are being trained. BPP University Law School prepares thousands of students each year for roles in professional legal practice which now has to include the effective use of AI. Jo-Anne Pugh, Dean of BPP Law School said, “BPP is excited to add Legora to the range of AI tools it offers to its students to enhance their professional skills and ensure they are desk-ready for the rapidly evolving AI transformation of modern legal practice”.


At King's and City, the program's impact comes into sharpest focus in the pro bono clinics. Students volunteer to take on real matters for people with limited access to legal assistance, spanning employment issues, criminal appeals, personal injury and more. With Legora, students raise the quality of their research, review, and drafting, extending the reach of clinics that provide a vital service to their communities. It is legal work that matters, done by students who are learning to practice at a higher level from day one.


Professor Dan Hunter, executive dean of the Dickson Poon School of Law at King's College London said, "AI is transforming the legal profession and our students have to learn how to navigate these changes. I'm proud to work with Legora and thrilled that our student clinics are now able to use Legora to aid those most in need of legal services. This initiative shows how AI can help the underserved in our community, while teaching our students how to take control of their careers."


"We're really pleased to be working with Legora and to allow our students to use legal AI as part of their clinical legal education. For us, it is not just about learning how to use the technology, but understanding when to use it, how to question it and how to exercise proper professional judgement. Those are increasingly important skills for students who will be entering a profession where AI is becoming part of everyday legal practice," said Sally Gill, Director of the City Community Legal Advice Centre at The City Law School.


"Working directly with the pro bono clinics, I get to see students put these tools to work on real cases, and the value is immediate," said Matthew Smith, Legal Engineer at Legora. "They are delivering high-quality legal help to people who need it most, from day one of their legal careers. That is exactly the kind of head start the Legal AI Scholars Program is designed to give them."


**About Legora**


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 130,000 legal professionals at more than 2,000 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.


Schools interested in joining the initiative may contact academic@legora.com or visit[legora.com/academic](https://legora.com/academic) for more information.
